question: Chenab river of north India originates from the confluence of which of the following two rivers?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandra and Bhaga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Chenab River** is one of the five major rivers in the **Punjab region, flowing through India and Pakistan**.
 
• It is produced by the confluence of two higher Himalayan headwaters**, Chandra and Bhaga**, in the Himachal Pradesh region of Lahaul and Spiti.
 
• Chenab flows through the Jammu region of Jammu and Kashmir, India, and into the Punjab plains of Pakistan, eventually joining the Indus River.
 
• Under the rules of the Indus Waters Treaty, Pakistan was given the Chenab's waters. Non-consumptive applications, such as power generating, are permitted in India. In Pakistan, the Chenab River is widely used for irrigation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The longest of the five tributaries of the** Indus River **that give Punjab its name is the** Sutlej River,** Ancient Greek Zaradros, Sanskrit Shutudri, or Shatadru.
 
• The primary tributaries of the Indus in Kashmir are the **Zaskar, Nubra, Shyok, and Hunza**.
 
• **The Nubra River is a river in Ladakh, India**, that flows through the Nubra Valley.
